paragraphs.text: A further effect is that people may become less willing to take part in similar activities. This matters because people can see whether their income covers essential needs. For example, a student can compare spending on transport, food and online orders before deciding where to cut back. If a negative experience prevents someone from trying again, that potential benefit may be lost. Repeated difficulties can also reduce confidence in the organisation or advice behind the activity.
paragraphs.noteVi: Theo dõi chi tiêu giúp thấy nhu cầu thiết yếu; kế hoạch phải có khoảng linh hoạt cho việc phát sinh.

paragraphs.label: Mở bài
paragraphs.text: Difficulties related to making time for hobbies can have effects beyond the activity itself. One important example is the possibility that an ambitious hobby plan can become another source of pressure. Looking at the causes and consequences can explain why a proposal that appears useful may produce a disappointing experience for some people.
paragraphs.noteVi: Xác định vấn đề, báo trước nguyên nhân và hệ quả.

paragraphs.label: Nguyên nhân
paragraphs.text: One reason for the difficulty is that people may compare their starting point with experienced hobbyists. This can help explain why an ambitious hobby plan can become another source of pressure. Consider the following situation: someone may stop practising music after trying to learn several difficult pieces in the first week. It shows that the problem is connected with the way the activity is organised, not only with an individual's attitude. Unless that underlying condition changes, asking people to try harder may have little effect.
paragraphs.noteVi: Giải thích cơ chế gây khó khăn.

paragraphs.label: Hệ quả trực tiếp
paragraphs.text: The immediate effect can be frustration and difficulty taking part. This is understandable because expensive equipment and demanding goals may make a beginner feel unsuccessful. A concrete example is that someone may stop practising music after trying to learn several difficult pieces in the first week. The person involved may then need to change plans, ask for additional help or look for a different way to meet the same need. The impact therefore extends beyond one unsuccessful attempt.

paragraphs.label: Hệ quả lâu dài
paragraphs.text: A further effect is that people may become less willing to take part in similar activities. This matters because a hobby can provide a break from work and routine responsibilities. For example, an office worker can spend one evening each week learning to draw with a small local group. If a negative experience prevents someone from trying again, that potential benefit may be lost. Repeated difficulties can also reduce confidence in the organisation or advice behind the activity.
